spec: Split text on whitespace and return the number of distinct words (an integer), treating words case-sensitively. An empty or whitespace-only string returns 0.
visible_tests: assert count_unique_words('the cat sat on the mat') == 5

spec: Split text on whitespace and find the words that occur exactly once. Return a sorted list of those words (case-sensitive, no duplicates since each occurs once anyway). An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty list.

Split text on whitespace and find the distinct words that occur at least k times. Return a sorted list of those words. If k is 0 or negative, every distinct word qualifies. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty list.
Find the value in items with the highest count. If several values tie for the highest count, return whichever of them appears first in the original list. The list is assumed non-empty.

Split text on whitespace and count words treating different letter casing as the same word (using the lowercase form as the key). Return a dict mapping each lowercased word to its total count. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty dict.

Given a list of dicts with numeric values, merge them all together by summing values for keys that appear in more than one dict. Return a single dict containing every key seen, with each mapped to the sum of its values across all input dicts. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of (group, item) tuples, determine for each group how many distinct items it contains (duplicates within the same group counted once). Return a dict mapping each group to its distinct item count. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of (group, item) tuples, build a nested dict where each group maps to a dict counting how many times each item occurred within that group. Return the nested dict. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a (possibly nested) dict d and a list of keys, walk into the dict following each key in turn (d[keys[0]][keys[1]]...). Return the final value reached, or None if at any step the current value is not a dict or does not contain the next key. An empty keys list returns d itself.
Given a dict whose values are either plain values or further nested dicts, count the total number of leaf values (non-dict values) anywhere in the structure, recursively. An empty dict returns 0.

Flatten a dict that may contain nested dicts as values into a single-level dict, joining the path of keys with '.' (e.g. {'a': {'b': 1}} becomes {'a.b': 1}). Leaf (non-dict) values are copied as-is. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Given a list of strings, count how many times each character appears across all of them combined. Return a dict mapping each distinct character to its total count. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Return a list of the k keys with the largest values in d, ordered by value descending and, for ties, by key ascending. If k exceeds the number of keys, return all keys in that order. An empty dict returns an empty list.

Return a list of the k keys with the smallest values in d, ordered by value ascending and, for ties, by key ascending. If k exceeds the number of keys, return all keys in that order. An empty dict returns an empty list.
Return a new dict containing only the entries of d whose key (a string) has length less than or equal to max_len. The original dict is unmodified. If nothing qualifies, return an empty dict.

Given a list of item names and a dict mapping some item names to a category string, count how many items fall into each category. Items not present in the categories dict are counted under 'other'. Return a dict mapping category to count. An empty items list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of (key, value) tuples, build a dict mapping each key to a sorted list of the distinct values associated with it. Duplicate (key, value) pairs contribute only one entry. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a dict mapping keys to lists of values, count the total number of times each value appears across all the lists combined (not deduplicated). Return a dict mapping each distinct value to its total count. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Split both text1 and text2 on whitespace and find the distinct words that appear in text1 but not in text2. Return a sorted list of those words. If every word of text1 also appears in text2, return an empty list.
visible_tests: assert unique_words_first_only('the cat sat', 'the dog sat') == ['cat']
assert unique_words_first_only('a b c', 'd e f') == ['a', 'b', 'c']

spec: Split both text1 and text2 on whitespace and count occurrences of each word in each. For every word that appears in either text, compute its count in text1 minus its count in text2 (treating a missing word as count 0). Return a dict mapping each such word to that difference.
visible_tests: assert word_count_difference('a a b', 'a b b') == {'a': 1, 'b': -1}

spec: Bucket each non-negative integer age into a decade label: '0-9', '10-19', ..., '90-99', or '100+' for ages 100 and above. Return a dict mapping each label that has at least one age to the count of ages in it (labels with no ages are omitted). An empty list returns an empty dict.
Classify each integer in nums as positive, negative, or zero. Return a dict with keys 'positive', 'negative', and 'zero' mapping to the counts of each (0 if none). An empty list returns all zeros.

Given a dict with values of possibly different types, count how many values belong to each Python type (using the type's __name__, e.g. 'int', 'str', 'list'). Return a dict mapping each type name found to its count. An empty dict returns an empty dict.
Given a dict with string keys and numeric values, sum the values of all keys that start with the given prefix. Return that sum (0 if no key matches, including for an empty dict).

Split the strings in the list into two groups based on whether their length is even or odd. Return a dict with keys 'even_length' and 'odd_length', each mapping to a sorted list of the matching strings. An empty list returns two empty lists.

Count how many times each character occurs in s, then keep only the characters that occur more than once. Return a dict mapping each such repeated character to its count. If no character repeats (including an empty string), return an empty dict.

Find the values in the list items that occur more than once. Return a sorted list of those distinct values (each listed once, regardless of how many times it repeats). An empty list, or a list with no repeats, returns an empty list.

Given a list (a sequence of hashable values), count how often each ordered pair of consecutive elements occurs, using a key formatted as '<from>-><to>' with the string forms of the elements. Return a dict mapping each such transition string to its count. A sequence with fewer than two elements returns an empty dict.

Group the keys of d by their value, then keep only the groups where two or more keys share that value. Return a dict mapping each such shared value to a sorted list of the keys that have it; values held by only one key are excluded. An empty dict, or one with no shared values, returns an empty dict.
Split text on whitespace and count how many of the resulting words have a length strictly greater than threshold. Return that count as an integer. An empty or whitespace-only string returns 0.

For each key present in both d1 and d2, take the smaller of the two values. Return a dict containing only those common keys mapped to that minimum; keys unique to either dict are excluded. If there are no common keys, return an empty dict.

Scan through items from left to right, and after including each element, determine the most frequent element among those seen so far (ties broken by the smallest element). Return a list containing this running mode after each step, so the result has the same length as items.

Group the integers in nums by their remainder when divided by the positive integer m (using Python's modulo, so remainders are always non-negative). Return a dict mapping each occupied remainder to a sorted list of the numbers that produced it. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list of (item, weight) tuples, sum the weight for each distinct item. Return a dict mapping each item to its total weight. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Count how many times each character in s occurs, but skip any character that is present in exclude (a string or list of characters to ignore). Return a dict mapping each remaining distinct character to its count. If every character is excluded, or s is empty, return an empty dict.
Count how many keys are present in both d1 and d2 but map to different values in each. Return that count as an integer. If there is no overlap, or all shared keys agree, return 0.
Count how many keys in d equal their own mapped value (a 'fixed point', e.g. {'a': 'a'}). Return that count as an integer. An empty dict, or one with no such keys, returns 0.

Split text on whitespace and group the words by their length. Within each length group, find the most frequent word (ties broken alphabetically). Return a dict mapping each word length present to that most frequent word of that length. An empty or whitespace-only string returns an empty dict.

Given a list of dicts with numeric values, find the keys that appear in two or more of the dicts. Return a dict mapping each such shared key to the sum of its values across every dict that contains it; keys that appear in only one dict are excluded. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a dict mapping item names to a category label, count how many items fall into each category. Return a dict mapping each category label to the number of items with that label. An empty dict returns an empty dict.
